chunks: From him, from Al-Mu'alla, from Al-Hasan, from Aban, from Abu Hashim who said:

When Ali (peace be upon him) was taken out, Fatima (peace be upon her) also came out, placing the shirt of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on her head, holding her two sons by the hand. So she said: 'What is it between me and you, O Abu Bakr? You want to orphan my two sons and widow me from my husband? By Allah! Had it not been a sin, I would have released my hair and cried out to my Lord!' So a man from the people said, 'What do you want from all this?' Then she took him by the hand and left with him.

key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ: Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.قَمِيصَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The shirt/tunic of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What did Fatima (peace be upon her) say to Abu Bakr when Ali (peace be upon him) was taken out?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the intimate connection between Fatima (peace be upon her) and the Prophet Muhammad through her wearing his *qamis*, symbolizing her inheriting his spiritual and physical presence during the pivotal moment of Ali's extraction. Her direct address to Abu Bakr underscores the immediate political and familial tensions following the Prophet's death, while her restraint from wailing—citing the fear of being a 'bad example' (*sayyi'ah*)—reflects the Shia emphasis on her dignified endurance (*sabr*) in the face of loss. The inclusion of this specific chain of transmission (*isnad*) in *Al-Kafi* serves to authenticate the domestic and emotional reality of the event within early Shia historiography.
